result.citation: San Diego Mun. Code § 98.1101 et seq. (Ord. O-21955 N.S.)
result.official_quote: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. For each month a violation of section 98.1103(b) exists or continues, and for each residential rental property a landlord uses an algorithmic device, it shall constitute a separate and distinct violation. A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord.
result.note: The card merges the definition (§ 98.1102), the prohibitions (§ 98.1103) and the remedies (§ 98.1104), so it now cites the whole Division 11 with 'et seq.' in place of a single section plus a 'see also' list, and the ordinance number is put in house form; the card's source D076 is only the unadopted draft (O-2025-107), so the quote comes from the adopted code text D074, which also makes attorney's fees two-way (prevailing landlord or tenant).
